findings.claim: Spec-7 (correctness-58) requires: 'Review-lane subagents must invoke the shared review skill with its no-context option so lanes receive zero doctrine injection, restoring the skill's own already-documented lanes-get-no-injection contract instead of silently receiving tens of kilobytes of unrequested doctrine per lane.' The v8.3 changelog entry (committed in this same diff range) implements exactly that: lane Skill invocation carries --no-context. But the very next version, v8.4 (also landed in this diff, changelog line: 'lane context model reversed: lanes now invoke the Skill tool BARE and receive the full doctrine injection (the v8.3 --no-context suppression is removed) — the intended model is every lane gets all the review context'), undoes it. At head commit 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e, SKILL-RAILROADREVIEW-CTX-002 (SKILL.md:159) reads 'every lane invokes the Skill tool bare (no args) and receives the full doctrine injection' and workflows/railroad-review.js:202 builds the lane prompt with 'Invoke the Skill tool with skill="railroad-review" — bare, no args; the hook injects your full review context'. No --no-context token exists anywhere in the shipped file (verified: grep for 'no-context'/'--no-context'/'bare' in the committed SKILL.md returns only this reversed wording). This is the opposite of what correctness-58 requires, landing in the same change that was supposed to deliver it.
findings.fix: Either restore the --no-context lane invocation (workflows/railroad-review.js lanePrompt, and SKILL-RAILROADREVIEW-CTX-002 in SKILL.md) per correctness-58, or — if the reversal to full-injection is a deliberate, later architectural decision — record that decision explicitly as superseding spec-7's correctness-58 (e.g. an errata/decision note) instead of silently landing the opposite of a stated requirement in the same diff.
findings.evidence: Re-read skills/quality/railroad-review/SKILL.md in full at commit 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e (git show) and workflows/railroad-review.js in full at the same commit; confirmed CTX-002 (line 159) and the lanePrompt() invocation text (line 202) both describe bare invocation + full injection, with no --no-context anywhere in either file. Cross-checked against the changelog.json entries for v8.3 and v8.4, which narrate the add-then-revert explicitly. This directly contradicts spec-7-raw's correctness-58 item, which is part of this round's given spec chain.

findings.claim: This diff adds smine-permissions as a fifth proposal-producing dimension (proposals/permissions.json), wired into PROPOSAL_DIMENSIONS (session-mine.js:45) and the parallel fan-out, consistent with /smine's documented --max-proposals-per-dimension cap (applies via the PROPOSAL_DIMENSIONS.has(name) check, which does include smine-permissions). But the Trim stage — which enforces /smine's --max-proposals-mined 'global cap on new proposals this run' (SKILL.md Args) — builds its enforcement prompt hardcoded to only three files: 'Across proposals/{routines,context,skills}.json, count proposals with status "proposed" and proposed = today' (session-mine.js:175-176). proposals/permissions.json is never named, so any new permissions proposals from this run are invisible to the Trim agent's count and removal logic. When --max-proposals-mined is set and smine-permissions produces proposals in the same run, the total count of new proposals created can exceed the stated global cap, because permissions.json's proposals are neither counted toward the cap nor eligible for the overflow removal the Trim stage performs.
findings.fix: Add proposals/permissions.json to the Trim stage prompt's file set in session-mine.js (line ~175): 'Across proposals/{routines,context,skills,permissions}.json, count proposals with status "proposed" and proposed = today', and include it in the overflow-removal instruction and kind-selection logic so permissions proposals are counted and trimmable like the other four dimensions.
findings.evidence: Re-read skills/smine/smine/workflows/session-mine.js in full: line 45 lists PROPOSAL_DIMENSIONS including 'smine-permissions'; lines 171-183 (Trim stage) construct the trim agent's prompt referencing only 'proposals/{routines,context,skills}.json' — permissions.json and (separately, correctly, since memory writes into context.json) memory's target are not named. Cross-checked skills/smine/smine-permissions/SKILL.md confirming proposals/permissions.json is a distinct, separate artifact from context.json/routines.json/skills.json, so it is not folded in by any of the three named globs. The omission is load-bearing: the Trim stage is the sole mechanical enforcement of the --max-proposals-mined global cap documented in skills/smine/smine/SKILL.md's Args section.
